parts:
Hi distancers, 

I have done fieldwork last week on three different forest type looking for the figs trees.  Each forest type has 5 replicates of which in total 15  transects (≥ 1km for each line-transect survey) were done.  

At the moment I am going to prepare my data before I run it in R.
After going through Chapter 7 online course on using ds package in R, I'm interested to run my analysis in R, which I can get varies plot in advance. However, I am still have a question on the data "Header/Field" of "Line transect.Length". by referring the formula, "Lenght" is referred to total Lenght of all transect. (or sorry if I am misunderstood the formula). If the total length is used, then, if I want to compare that three different forest type, so it means "Line transect.Length" of each forest type is the total length of all transect within each forest type?. 


Also, need confirmation, the "Header/Field" of "Region.Area". is it the value of a=2wL(area of covered) or A (size of study region)?

I have attached here my csv data. Is my data arrangement are correct?

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] How to organize data for Distance in R. Urgent
parts:
Suzi

Your data are *almost* ready for analysis by the Distance package.  You do need to be specific about the field names, use ?flatfile for details.

Each row of the data table corresponds to one observation and must have a the following columns:

Each row of the data table corresponds to one observation and must have a the following columns:


distance        observed distance to object
Sample.Label    Identifier for the sample (transect id)
Effort          effort for this transect (e.g. line transect length or number of times point transect was visited)
Region.Label    label for a given stratum (see below)
Area            area of the strata

You also have several empty rows at the bottom of your data that I deleted this way:

suzi <- read.csv("C:/Users/eric/Documents/My Distance Projects/Full data for Distance in R.csv")
names(suzi) <- c("Region.Label","Area","Sample.Label","Effort","distance")
suzi <- suzi[1:140,]

However, I think you might not have specified all of your measurements in the same units.  I suspect you have specified effort and distance in meters.  However, I don't know the units you have used to specify area.  The simplest thing for you to do is specify this in square meters.

To your questions defining items (after you have read Chapter 7):

"Effort" is specified for each transect; for example if you have transects A, B, C and D with lengths of 1200m, 1000m, 1500m, and 1100m; those values of effort would be provided for each transect.  So effort is transect-specific, not stratum-specific.

The "Area" specified is the size of the stratum, not the size of the area covered in the stratum; in the notation you use, it is A.
